findings.reason: naming `_launch_queued`/`_node_from_pointer` as the place the steering file is re-read tells the node where the file read and the digest override belong; without it the node can wire the edit verbs and a digest that still records the text captured at queue time.
findings.text: §5 says "admission reads it at launch" and names `_store_brief` only as the function that stores the copy; it names no call site, and the real queued launch is `_launch_queued` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:158`), which rebuilds the node from the queued pointer via `_node_from_pointer` (`:106-140`, carrying the queue-time `brief`, `brief_sha256` and `brief_path`), deletes the pointer and calls `dispatch()`, whose `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1816` stores `node.brief` — the queue-time text — so an implementer following the existing path reproduces the copy-at-dispatch defect §1 measures

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching §5 has no scope to grant or audit against, so two workers on neighbouring sections can be handed the same module and the manifest cannot be checked against a declared scope.
findings.text: §5's mechanism spans `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py` (the `_store_brief` copy), the launch path in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, the CLI surface in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` and its MCP `crew` action, plus a new test file, yet §5 declares neither write paths nor where its gate log goes, while §2 (`:49`) and §8 (`:80`) both carry a "Write paths:" line and §2 also says every log is under the run directory

findings.reason: the edit verb and the launch-time read must resolve the same file, and the three candidate directories differ in who may write them — a coordinator can write a checkout's `docs/state/` but the global crew directory is where a worker is fenced out — so an implementer choosing a different one from the plan's intent changes both the durable path and whether the coordinator can edit it at all.
findings.text: §5 says a steering file is "a markdown file the coordinator writes under the project's crew state", and no path of that name exists in the tree: a project's state lives at `docs/state/<project>/` in its own checkout (`reckon/flight.py:488-499`) and the global crew directory `~/.config/reckon/crew/` holds no per-project steering tree

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §5's steering file is placed "under the project's crew state" and no such path exists under that name; `_store_brief` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2241`) and `crew view live --phase` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:238`) both resolve, and `position`/`rank` are already on a queued placement (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1043-1044`) as §5 asserts.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's measure is a recorded digest matching edited text, plus three refusals that can fail (an edit naming a model its lane does not declare, an edit on a launched request, a steering file made invalid while queued), so the section has a negative control that would redden if the guard did not fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §5 is the only implementable section in the wave that declares no write paths and no gate log path, while its mechanism reaches at least four files.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose; its symbols are `crew queue edit | reprioritise | drop`, named by what they do.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 names no caller for the launch-time read, and the launch path it would naturally attach to carries the queue-time brief, so the mechanism as written can be implemented into exactly the copy-at-dispatch behaviour the section exists to remove.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the launch-time binding, the digest it records and the edit verbs that act on the same request before launch are one deliverable: the digest is what makes an edit observable, and no clause can be closed independently of it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `s5` declares `depends-on: [s2]` and every section that consumes its verbs is transitively ordered after it (`s4` depends on `s5`, and `s7`, `s10`, `s15`, `s13` reach `s5` through `s4`), so `crew queue reprioritise` and `crew queue edit` are both defined before the sections that use them.
